# Athene groups AI financing exposures by underlying counterparty credit


By OpenTools Team


The issuer separates shared‑credit aggregation from funded positions, commitments and whole‑project capitalization.


##


Count shared credit


Athene’s[presentation published October 30](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_b99908eeea79fb507cc96a8cb1a307f0/athene/db/2271/22574/pdf/Athene%27s_Role_in_Financing_AI-Related_Infrastructure_FINAL.pdf) says it combines bonds, lease‑backed loans, asset‑backed securities and guarantees when fulfilling an obligation primarily relies on the same counterparty’s credit. Single‑issuer limits apply to aggregated holdings. Different financing wrappers can therefore retain shared credit dependence.


##


Read the position date


Its relevant funded‑position tables use September 30 balances, gross of noncontrolling interests in ACRA, Athene’s co‑investment reinsurance affiliates. These differ from whole‑project capitalization and committed amounts. The publication describes Athene’s approach; it does not establish new October 30 lending or a newly adopted practice.


Original explanation of Athene’s stated approach: shared counterparty credit is aggregated across financing structures. No holdings or investment outcomes depicted.
